caption_hook: Idaho has black lava fields, a giant granite heart and some of the oldest rock in the West.

layers.name: SNAKE RIVER BASALT
layers.what: Along a long crack called the Great Rift, lava spilled across southern Idaho as recently as 2,000 years ago. It left lava tubes, cinder cones and fields of jagged black rock.
layers.bonus: Apollo astronauts trained at Craters of the Moon in 1969 before heading to the real Moon.

layers.name: SNAKE RIVER RHYOLITE
layers.hook: The trail of a hot spot
layers.what: As North America slid over the Yellowstone hot spot, gigantic eruptions blanketed southern Idaho in glassy ash and lava. Younger basalt later buried most of it.
layers.bonus: Shoshone Falls, at 212 ft, drops over this rock and is taller than Niagara.

layers.name: IDAHO BATHOLITH
layers.hook: A mountain range of frozen magma
layers.what: Molten rock welled up beneath ancient volcanoes and cooled into a vast mass of granite. It underlies much of the wild, rugged mountain country of central Idaho.
layers.bonus: It is one of the largest exposed bodies of granite in North America.

layers.name: PHOSPHORIA FORMATION
layers.what: Cold, nutrient-rich water welled up in an ancient sea, feeding plankton that piled up as phosphate-rich mud. Today it is mined near Soda Springs to make fertilizer.
layers.bonus: Soda Springs' famous geyser was an accident, set off by drilling in 1937.

layers.name: BELT SUPERGROUP
layers.hook: Mud and sand of a lost sea
layers.what: A mile-deep stack of mud and sand settled in a vast shallow sea, then hardened into slate and quartzite. Folded and faulted, it forms the mountains of the Idaho panhandle.
layers.bonus: Mines in this rock made the Silver Valley one of the richest silver districts ever.

layers.name: THE BASEMENT
layers.what: In southern Idaho, granite and gneiss about 2.5 billion years old poke up at City of Rocks. Weathering has shaped it and its younger granite neighbors into domes and towers.
layers.bonus: Wagon trains on the California Trail rolled right through City of Rocks.
